No. STOP You can’t take the credit." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A: "Use this worksheet only if you answered “No” to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A, line 2. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/eic.json`; 1,382 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 161 partial records; 2,043 comparisons): 1,824 of 2,043 agree; 78 project-unknown, 66 candidate-shows-skipped, 46 candidate-unknown, 28 candidate-refuses, 1 project-refuses; on returns the full interview completes: 21 candidate-shows-skipped, 13 candidate-unknown. Every completed-return difference was read with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-eic/eic.full.json): (a) 21 candidate-shows-skipped, the reply looking line 2 up after a STOP, where the project hides it: Step 1 question 1 (classm.f4952.2 and .deepseek $308.00, line 11b $64,348.06 married filing jointly), Step 1 question 2 (stage13.eic_spouse_no_ssn $649.00, audit.eic.filer_without_eic_ssn $4,060.00), Step 2 (stage9.eic.investment_income $1,369.00, stage16.cleanup.mut.clwb_three_figured $1,294.00), Steps 3 and 4 (stage9.eic.no_child.over65, .under25, .abroad, .qc_of_another $308.00 each; stage9.s8812.three_children.withholding_exceeds.no_eic $2,261.00) and generated 148, 175, 179, 269, 314, 346, 348, 373, 421, 439; the reply's own eic.credit is $0.00 on every one (no credit difference); (b) 13 candidate-unknown dependent.us_half: the reply's Step 1 limit is chosen by its count of qualifying children with valid SSNs (eic.h_limit through eic.h_kids and dependent.eic_ssn_child), which needs each dependent's dependent.us_half even where line 11b is at or above the largest limit and question 1 is No for any count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need is a model error (README) (stage8.hoh.child.ctc, stage8.single.dependent.boundaries, stage8.single.dependent.students_and_age17, stage8.single.dependent.household_and_ssn, audit.dependent.listed_not_dependent_no_tin and audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (line 11b $120,000.00), stage8.single.phaseout.partial and audit.household.single_community_property ($215,300.00); stage13.ctc_spouse_ssn, stage13.odc_spouse_no_tin and stage13.ctc_spouse_no_id (married filing jointly, $120,000.00); stage8.single.taxpayer_without_tin and stage8.single.taxpayer_without_work_ssn ($120,000.00)). Off completed returns: the 78 project-unknowns are no-band lookups of the project's line 2 on refused returns (hidden there), and the refusals are cited gates on refused returns: scope. Project stands.

No. STOP You can't take the credit." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A: "Use this worksheet only if you answered “No” to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A, line 2: "If line 2 is zero, STOP You can't take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,325 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 110 partial records; 1,935 comparisons): 1,683 of 1,935 agree; 66 candidate-shows-skipped (22 on completed returns), 46 candidate-unknown (13 on completed returns), 27 candidate-refuses, 17 project-refuses, 96 project-unknown. The candidate looks up line 2 on every return. Shown after a STOP: classm.f4952.2.deepseek (completed) hidden, candidate $308.00; classm.f4952.2 likewise. The candidate-unknown are the child-count limit unknowns of eic.credit (classm.f8995a.1, dependent[dep_c].us_half). The 96 project-unknown are all on refused returns where eic.eligible, the line's shown_when, itself refuses (triage counts a line as shown when its shown_when itself refuses, T-070 (2)): classm.dependent.2.deepseek (eic.eligible refused on div.bad_components) has line 1 $239,545.00, above the table ("no band"), and the candidate $0.00; on a return where eic.eligible is true, Step 5, question 3 (eic.step5_income, earned income below the limit) keeps line 1 inside the table, so no reachable return shows it. The refusals on both sides are cited gates on refused returns (scope). No value difference. Round 2 of Stage 19: the only eic change since round 4 is BUG-0195, the wording of eic.us_home (i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 3: "Was your main home, and your spouse's if filing a joint return, in the United States for more than half of 2025?"), which the project label and question now quote; it changes no expression, and no difference here turns on it.

No. STOP You can't take the credit." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A: "Use this worksheet only if you answered “No” to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A, line 2: "If line 2 is zero, STOP You can't take the credit." The candidate looks up line 2 on every return; the project hides it unless Steps 1 to 5 pass. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,099 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 132 partial records; 1,731 comparisons): 1,375 of 1,731 agree; 64 candidate-shows-skipped (26 on completed returns), 44 value, 49 candidate-unknown, 26 candidate-refuses, 101 project-unknown, 72 project-refuses. Witness: classm.sd.1 (completed; head of household, line 11b $168,227.38, Step 1 question 1 STOP) hidden, candidate $2,798.00. The candidate-unknown are its eic.h_limit and child count needed above every Step 1 limit (classm.f4952.1), a model error as on eic.credit. The value differences on returns the project completes or leaves incomplete are all Worksheet B filers (eic.self_employed true): the project's printed line 2 also carries Worksheet B line 7 (cite: "Worksheet A lines 2 to 6 are Worksheet B lines 7 to 11"), which the candidate's Worksheet A line cannot express; interface gap, as in round 2. The value differences on refused returns are Worksheet B values or lines whose shown_when itself refuses or is unknown (classm.sc.1: eic.eligible refuses on person[spouse].f8889[hsa].excess), which triage counts as shown; no amount is filed (scope). Witnesses: classm.s8812.3 (completed) project $300.00 (Worksheet B line 7), candidate $0.00; classm.f8880.1 project $0.00, candidate $2,798.00. The project-unknown and project-refuses are on returns the project refuses (scope). The project-refuses are cited gates on the Worksheet B side of the merged line (s179.multi, person[taxpayer].se_screened, Schedule C vehicle and home-office gates) and the candidate-refuses are s8812.combat_pay and the dependent other_claimant and married gates, all on returns the project refuses (scope).

No. STOP You can't take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,111 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 136 partial records; 1,747 comparisons): 1,653 of 1,747 agree; 50 candidate-unknown (13 on completed returns), 35 candidate-refuses, 4 project-refuses, 5 value (all on refused returns). The candidate's conditions read eic.h_s1q1, so candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_s1q1, which compares line 11b with a limit chosen by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs (eic.h_limit), so it needs each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half and the rest) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and the question is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in round 3. Witness: classm.f4952.1, project no, candidate unknown. The value differences are generated returns that answer married filing separately with household.married false; the candidate reads "married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately" from household.married, the project from the status (eic.married_rules); i1040gi p. 41, Step 3, question 3 / Step 4, question 1: "Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household?" -- a married-filing-separately filer is married. All are refused returns, so no box is filed (as ruled for the same reading in round 2, generated 71). Witness: generated 71 (no qualifying child, status married filing separately, household.married false, line 11b negative): project no (Step 4, question 1 "Yes. STOP You can't take the credit", no 27c instruction), candidate yes through its Worksheet B line 4b STOP; generated 239, 246, 323 and 480 are the same pattern. The candidate-refuses (dependent other_claimant and married-child gates, i1040gi p. 44) and the 4 project-refuses (Form 2555, Form 8814, sa.dependent and Step 1 question 3 gates, cited) are on refused returns: scope. No. STOP You can’t take the credit." executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/eic.json`; 1,382 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 161 partial records; 2,043 comparisons): 1,957 of 2,043 agree; 45 candidate-unknown, 40 candidate-refuses, 1 project-refuses; on returns the full interview completes: 13 candidate-unknown. Every completed-return difference was read with the witness cap lifted (triage.mjs run directly; scratch /tmp/adj-fixr2-dependent-eic/eic.full.json): the 13 completed candidate-unknowns are dependent.us_half: the reply's Step 1 limit is chosen by its count of qualifying children with valid SSNs (eic.h_limit through eic.h_kids and dependent.eic_ssn_child), which needs each dependent's dependent.us_half even where line 11b is at or above the largest limit and question 1 is No for any count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need is a model error (README). No. STOP You can't take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,325 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 110 partial records; 1,935 comparisons): 1,847 of 1,935 agree; no value difference; 46 candidate-unknown (13 on completed returns), 32 candidate-refuses, 10 project-refuses, all refusals on refused returns. The candidate's conditions read the same child-count limit as eic.credit, so: The candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_limit / eic.h_agi_ok, which choose the Step 1 limit by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs, so they need each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and question 1 is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in rounds 3 and 4. Witness: classm.f8995a.1 project no, candidate unknown. The candidate-refuses (dependent.married, dependent.other_claimant: classm.f8880.4, classm.carloan.1, classm.tcw.10 to .13) and the project-refuses (sa.excluded_income on classm.eic.6 and stage9.eic.refuse.form2555, i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 3; scope.other_line16 on stage9.eic.refuse.form8814; sa.dependent on stage9.eic.refuse.dependent_of_another; scope.other_income on stage9.eic.refuse.other_income.schedule1_unanswered) are cited gates on refused returns: scope. The married-filing-separately reading through household.married that gave the round 4 value differences is gone: the candidate now reads the filing status. Round 2 of Stage 19: the only eic change since round 4 is BUG-0195, the wording of eic.us_home (i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 3: "Was your main home, and your spouse's if filing a joint return, in the United States for more than half of 2025?"), which the project label and question now quote; it changes no expression, and no difference here turns on it. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 43, Line 27c: "Check the box on line 27c if you do not want to claim the earned income credit or if you have been instructed to check the box in the instructions for line 27a." i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 1: "If, in 2025: 3 or more children who have valid SSNs lived with you, is the amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b, less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly)? ... No. STOP You can't take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,099 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 132 partial records; 1,731 comparisons): 1,631 of 1,731 agree; no value difference; 48 candidate-unknown (13 on completed returns), 51 candidate-refuses, 1 project-refuses. The candidate's 27c conditions read eic.h_pre and eic.h_agi_ok, so it inherits the same unknowns. The candidate-unknown come from its helper eic.h_pre, which needs the child count (for its income limit) and investment income (f1040.line2a) before the Step 1, question 1 STOP that line 11b alone decides when it is at or above the largest limit; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README). Witnesses: classm.f4952.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project 0, candidate unknown; audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (completed; line 11b $120,000.00) candidate unknown (dependent eic_ssn and us_half, f1040.tax_exempt_interest, eic.qc_of_another not supplied). The 51 candidate-refuses are scope: its declared gates on eic.h_pre (sa.excluded_income, scope.other_line16) and the dependent other_claimant and married gates it reaches through the child count fire only on returns the project refuses (classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3, classm.tcw.10). The project refusal (stage9.eic.refuse.dependent_of_another, candidate no) is the cited sa.dependent gate (i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 6; scope). Project stands.

No. STOP You can’t take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/eic.json`; 1,374 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 124 partial records; 1,998 comparisons; every completed-return difference inspected with the 6-witness cap lifted, T-083): 1,914 of 1,998 agree; 1 value, 46 candidate-unknown (13 on completed returns), 26 candidate-refuses, 11 project-refuses. The 13 completed candidate-unknowns are the eic.credit child-count limit unknowns (dependent.us_half), all on returns above the largest Step 1 limit (line 11b $120,000.00 or $215,300.00; stage13.ctc_spouse_ssn, stage13.odc_spouse_no_tin, stage13.ctc_spouse_no_id married filing jointly above $68,675.00): model error. The one value (generated 480, refused; project no, candidate yes) is a married filing separately filer with household.married false whom the candidate carries past Step 4, question 1 to a Worksheet A line 2 of zero: Its Step 3/4 married test (eic.h_married_sep) requires household.married to be true even for married filing separately, so a separate filer recorded as unmarried passes Step 4, question 1; a married filing separately status is married by definition, and the project tests the status itself (eic.married_rules). Refusals are cited gates on refused returns (scope). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 1: "If, in 2025: 3 or more children who have valid SSNs lived with you, is the amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b, less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly)? ... No. STOP You can't take the credit." i1040gi p. 40, Step 2, question 2: "Is your investment income more than $11,950?" Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,111 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 136 partial records; 1,747 comparisons): 1,630 of 1,747 agree; no value difference; 40 candidate-unknown (8 on completed returns), 65 candidate-refuses (all on refused returns), 9 project-unknown, 3 project-refuses. The candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_s1q1, which compares line 11b with a limit chosen by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs (eic.h_limit), so it needs each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half and the rest) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and the question is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in round 3. Witnesses: classm.f4952.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project $0.00, candidate unknown (dependent[dep_c].us_half); classm.f4952.2 (incomplete) likewise. The candidate-refuses are its declared gates (eic.h_dep_screen: a child who is the qualifying child of another person, married, or under the divorced-parents rule; sa.excluded_income; scope.other_line16) on returns the project also refuses (classm.tcw.10, classm.carloan.1, classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3): scope. The 3 project-refuses are cited gates (i8889 HSA screen, retirement special exceptions, sa.dependent at i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 6 on stage9.eic.refuse.dependent_of_another): scope. The 9 project-unknown (stage14.ho.gross_limit, audit.sa.negative_agi_medical) withhold f1040.tax_exempt_interest, part of the Step 2 investment income the interview asks of every filer; the candidate reaches $0 only because its eligibility test fails first (representation). The T-071 change (ambiguity link on eic.separated_box) does not touch this line. Project stands.

No. STOP You can’t take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/eic.json`; 1,374 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 124 partial records; 1,998 comparisons; every completed-return difference inspected with the 6-witness cap lifted, T-083): 1,906 of 1,998 agree; 3 value, 38 candidate-unknown (8 on completed returns, 18 incomplete, 12 refused), 38 candidate-refuses, 9 project-unknown, 4 project-refuses. The completed candidate-unknowns are its Step 1 limit chosen by the count of qualifying children (eic.h_limit / eic.h_agi_ok), which needs each dependent's dependent.us_half even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and question 1 is No for any count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. All 8 completed ones checked: stage8.hoh.child.ctc, stage8.single.dependent.boundaries, stage8.single.dependent.students_and_age17, stage8.single.dependent.household_and_ssn, audit.dependent.listed_not_dependent_no_tin and audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property have line 11b $120,000.00, stage8.single.phaseout.partial and audit.household.single_community_property $215,300.00, against a largest limit of $61,555.00. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need is a model error (README), as in Stage 19 round 2. The 3 value differences (generated 246, 288 and 323; project $0.00, candidate $205.00 / $538.00 / $94.00) are refused returns of married filing separately filers without a qualifying child and household.married false: Its Step 3/4 married test (eic.h_married_sep) requires household.married to be true even for married filing separately, so a separate filer recorded as unmarried passes Step 4, question 1; a married filing separately status is married by definition, and the project tests the status itself (eic.married_rules). i1040gi p. 41, Step 4, question 1: "Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household? No. Continue Yes. STOP You can’t take the credit." The 38 candidate-refuses are its declared gates (dependent.other_claimant, dependent.married, sa.excluded_income) on returns the project also refuses: scope. The 9 project-unknown withhold f1040.tax_exempt_interest (7 incomplete; Step 2 needs it, representation) or are partial records withholding eic.qc_of_another / eic.us_home on refused classm.asset.4. The 4 project-refuses are cited screens (scope.other_line16, sa.dependent, f8889 and retirement screens). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 1: "If, in 2025: 3 or more children who have valid SSNs lived with you, is the amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b, less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly)? ... No. STOP You can't take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,325 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 110 partial records; 1,935 comparisons): 1,830 of 1,935 agree; no value difference; 38 candidate-unknown (8 on completed returns), 55 candidate-refuses (all on refused returns), 9 project-unknown, 3 project-refuses. The candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_limit / eic.h_agi_ok, which choose the Step 1 limit by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs, so they need each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and question 1 is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in rounds 3 and 4. Witnesses: classm.f8995a.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project $0.00, candidate unknown (dependent[dep_c].us_half); tcw.hoh.b1 (incomplete) likewise. The candidate-refuses are its declared gates (scope.other_line16 on classm.clcw26.3.deepseek and classm.eic.7.deepseek; dependent.married, i1040gi p. 44, Married child, on classm.f8880.4; dependent.other_claimant, p. 44, Qualifying child of more than one person, on classm.carloan.1), all on returns the project also refuses: scope. The 3 project-refuses are cited gates (i8889 HSA screen on stage16.cleanup.refuse.f8889.screen_no_amounts; Form 1099-R special exceptions; sa.dependent, i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 6, on stage9.eic.refuse.dependent_of_another): scope. The 9 project-unknown (stage14.ho.gross_limit, stage14.s179.income_limit, audit.sa.negative_agi_medical) withhold f1040.tax_exempt_interest, part of the Step 2 investment income the interview asks of every filer; the candidate reaches $0 only because its eligibility test fails first (representation). Round 2 of Stage 19: the only eic change since round 4 is BUG-0195, the wording of eic.us_home (i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 3: "Was your main home, and your spouse's if filing a joint return, in the United States for more than half of 2025?"), which the project label and question now quote; it changes no expression, and no difference here turns on it. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 1: "If, in 2025: 3 or more children who have valid SSNs lived with you, is the amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b, less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly)? ... No. STOP You can't take the credit." i1040gi p. 40, Step 2, question 2: "Is your investment income more than $11,950? Yes. Continue". Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,099 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 132 partial records; 1,731 comparisons): 1,628 of 1,731 agree; no value difference; 41 candidate-unknown (8 on completed returns), 51 candidate-refuses, 8 project-unknown, 3 project-refuses. The candidate-unknown come from its helper eic.h_pre, which needs the child count (for its income limit) and investment income (f1040.line2a) before the Step 1, question 1 STOP that line 11b alone decides when it is at or above the largest limit; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README). Witnesses: classm.f4952.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project 0, candidate unknown; audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (completed; line 11b $120,000.00) candidate unknown (dependent eic_ssn and us_half, f1040.tax_exempt_interest, eic.qc_of_another not supplied). The 51 candidate-refuses are scope: its declared gates on eic.h_pre (sa.excluded_income, scope.other_line16) and the dependent other_claimant and married gates it reaches through the child count fire only on returns the project refuses (classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3, classm.tcw.10). The 3 project-refuses are cited gates (person[taxpayer].f8889[hsa].unsupported, retirement[p].special, and sa.dependent, i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 6, on stage9.eic.refuse.dependent_of_another), scope. The 8 project-unknown (stage14.ho.gross_limit, audit.sa.negative_agi_medical) are incomplete records that withhold f1040.line2a, the Step 2 investment-income answer the interview asks of every filer; the candidate reaches 0 there only because both of its worksheet paths are false (representation). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 41, Step 3, question 6: "No. Check the box in the Dependents section that discusses the special rule for separated spouses"; i1040gi p. 44, Special rule for separated spouses: "If you are married, but not filing a joint return, had a qualifying child who lived with you ... If you meet these requirements, make sure you check the box in the Dependents section that discusses the special rule for separated spouses". Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,099 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 132 partial records; 1,731 comparisons): 1,675 of 1,731 agree; no value difference; 3 candidate-unknown (1 on a completed return), 51 candidate-refuses, 2 project-refuses. The candidate now limits the box to married filers filing separately or as head of household (eic.h_married_ns), as the project does, but conditions it on eic.h_pre. The candidate-unknown come from its helper eic.h_pre, which needs the child count (for its income limit) and investment income (f1040.line2a) before the Step 1, question 1 STOP that line 11b alone decides when it is at or above the largest limit; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README). Witnesses: classm.f4952.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project 0, candidate unknown; audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (completed; line 11b $120,000.00) candidate unknown (dependent eic_ssn and us_half, f1040.tax_exempt_interest, eic.qc_of_another not supplied). The 51 candidate-refuses are scope: its declared gates on eic.h_pre (sa.excluded_income, scope.other_line16) and the dependent other_claimant and married gates it reaches through the child count fire only on returns the project refuses (classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3, classm.tcw.10). The 2 project-refuses are cited gates (HSA unsupported, retirement special) on refused returns. Project stands.

Continue No. Skip questions 4 and 5; go to question 6"; question 6: "No. Check the box in the Dependents section that discusses the special rule for separated spouses"; amb.2025.separated_spouses_box (chosen reading: the box only on that Step 3 path). Triage executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/eic.json`; 1,374 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 124 partial records; 1,998 comparisons; every completed-return difference inspected with the 6-witness cap lifted, T-083): 1,954 of 1,998 agree; 4 value, 3 candidate-unknown (1 on a completed return), 26 candidate-refuses, 11 project-refuses; all differences but one unknown are on refused returns. The 4 values (classm.eic.8 and .deepseek, generated 115 and 415; project yes, candidate no) are married filing separately filers with household.married false and eic.same_home false: Its Step 3/4 married test (eic.h_married_sep) requires household.married to be true even for married filing separately, so a separate filer recorded as unmarried passes Step 4, question 1; a married filing separately status is married by definition, and the project tests the status itself (eic.married_rules). The completed unknown (audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property, line 11b $120,000.00) is the child-count limit unknown of eic.credit. Refusals are cited gates on refused returns (scope). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 41, Step 3, question 3: "Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household? Yes. Continue No. Skip questions 4 and 5; go to question 6"; question 6: "No. Check the box in the Dependents section that discusses the special rule for separated spouses"; p. 44, Special rule for separated spouses. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,325 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 110 partial records; 1,935 comparisons): 1,891 of 1,935 agree; no value difference; 3 candidate-unknown (1 on a completed return), 32 candidate-refuses and 9 project-refuses, all on refused returns. The candidate restricts the box to a married filer filing separately or as head of household who passed questions 4 and 5 and answers No to question 6, which is the project's eic.separated_box term for term (eic.married_rules, eic.step3_married, eic.qc_of_another, after eic.reached_step3) and the chosen reading of amb.2025.separated_spouses_box. The unknowns are the child-count limit again. The candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_limit / eic.h_agi_ok, which choose the Step 1 limit by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs, so they need each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and question 1 is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in rounds 3 and 4. Witness: audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (completed) project no, candidate unknown (dependent[child].us_half). The refusals are cited gates on refused returns (dependent.married, dependent.other_claimant for the candidate; sa.excluded_income on classm.eic.6, scope.other_line16, scope.other_income for the project): scope. Round 2 of Stage 19: the only eic change since round 4 is BUG-0195, the wording of eic.us_home (i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 3: "Was your main home, and your spouse's if filing a joint return, in the United States for more than half of 2025?"), which the project label and question now quote; it changes no expression, and no difference here turns on it. Project stands.
